subject.title: feat(android): Talk camera flip control and microphone selection

question: Should OpenClaw ship persistent Talk camera and microphone preferences that influence agent capture defaults after the shared invocation semantics and physical-device behavior are proven?
rationale: This is a new persistent Android product surface, and the requested scope—whether a user-selected Talk camera should become the default for agent camera tools—needs explicit product ownership in addition to the mechanical caller repair.

options.title: Sponsor the repaired preference model
options.body: Preserve omitted facing through the agent media path, retain explicit agent overrides, and require Android device proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the feature scope
options.body: Keep the controls local to a separately defined Talk capture flow rather than changing the default behavior of agent camera tools.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Defer persistent camera and microphone selection until Android Talk preference semantics are explicitly designed and validated.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the repaired preference model
recommendation.body: Preserve omitted facing through the agent media path, retain explicit agent overrides, and require Android device proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR's Android feature implementation and stated product behavior originate with this contributor; ownership confidence is limited without current-main history access.
